svg.title: How Token Visualizer splits a prompt into tokens, counts them and measures savings
svg.desc: A real run on examples/support-prompt.txt with the GPT-4o tokenizer. Line 2 is cut into 16 tokens with their IDs. Line counts are 12, 16, 17, 18, 7, total 70 tokens, 357 characters, estimated $0.0021. Swapping wordy phrases and re-tokenizing takes it from 70 to 61 tokens.
svg.text: How Token Visualizer counts and costs a prompt
Real run: token-visualizer examples/support-prompt.txt -m gpt-4o (tiktoken o200k_base)
The model's tokenizer cuts each line into tokens (numbered pieces)
Line 2: In order to help the customer, read their whole message carefully before you answer.
16 tokens. · is a space: most tokens carry the space before the word. The number is the token ID.
Count every line, then the whole prompt
bar colour: green under 25 tokens, yellow 25 to 50, red over 50
at the old GPT-4 price, $0.03 per 1K
Swap wordy phrases, re-tokenize, and measure what you saved
The five phrases it knows: in order to, due to the fact that, at this point in time, for the purpose of, in the event that.
Extra spaces and blank lines are squeezed too. Then the new text goes through the same tokenizer again.
Colours match the terminal output. Numbers from a real run of token_visualizer.py.
